**Observations from test image:**
- Corn leaf with large, elongated tan/brown lesions
- Lesions are irregular-elongated, tan/straw-colored centers with darker brown borders
- One lesion spans diagonally across the upper leaf margin; another elongated lesion lower on the blade
- No rust pustules, no small circular spots, no vascular discoloration

**Comparison with Northern Corn Leaf Blight reference:**
- Reference shows the same large, cigar/spindle-shaped elongated tan lesions running parallel to leaf veins
- Same tan-brown coloration with darker margins
- Same size and orientation pattern on the leaf blade

The elongated, cigar-shaped tan lesions are the hallmark of Northern Corn Leaf Blight (*Exserohilum turcicum*). The lesions in the test image match closely — large (several cm), tan/straw centers, darker brown borders, oriented along the leaf axis.
